title: SocialDF: Benchmark Dataset and Detection Model for Mitigating Harmful Deepfake Content on Social Media Platforms
positive_applications:
Used for misinformation mitigation, fact-checking, content verification,
and protection of public figures.
ethical_concerns:
Highlights misuse of generative tools to impersonate individuals
and spread misinformation
detection_limitations:
Existing lip-sync detection models like LipFD fail in the wild:
51.24% accuracy on SocialDF.

Failures due to:
multiple speakers
occlusions
scene cuts
rapid head movement
inconsistent lighting
short-form platform artifacts
robustness:
Evaluated on noisy, real-world, highly compressed mobile-platform videos.

Multimodal LLM detection framework shows strong robustness:
DeepSeek R-1 8B achieves 90.4% accuracy and 0.93 F1-score.

Outperforms traditional lip-sync baselines across diverse creators, languages, and content types.
data_collection:
Video Collection:
Videos scraped from public social media platforms (Instagram-style short videos).
Filtering based on hashtags: #deepfake, #faceswap, #parody.
Verification via captions, uploader descriptions, and comment threads.
Final dataset: 2,126 videos (1,071 real / 1,055 fake).

Audio Collection:
Extracted audio from videos using standard processing.
Transcribed with Whisper V3 Turbo for speech content understanding.

Image / Face Regions:
Faces detected using YOLOv8.
Face embeddings computed with FaceNet for speaker/identity matching.

Text Collection:
Captions, descriptions, and audio transcripts combined as textual modality.
Used for multimodal reasoning in the LLM detection pipeline.
detection_models:
Deep Learning: multimodal pipeline using YOLO (face detection),
FaceNet (facial embeddings), Whisper V3 Turbo (ASR), and
multi-agent LLM (DeepSeek R-1, Llama 3.3, Qwen 2.5)
datasets:
SocialDF (proposed); also compared against
FakeAVCeleb, LAV-DF, AV-Deepfake1M, and DeepSpeak v1.0
feature_extraction:
YOLO (face detection),
FaceNet (identity embeddings),
Whisper (speech-to-text).

No hand-crafted features.
sota_baselines: LipFD (used for baseline)
summary:
The paper introduces SocialDF, a benchmark dataset of 2,126 videos (1,071 real / 1,055 fake) collected
from Instagram-style platforms. The proposed fact-checking pipeline first detects and identifies individuals
via YOLO and FaceNet, transcribes speech using Whisper, and then applies a multi-agent LLM framework
(DeepSeek R-1, Llama 3.3, Qwen 2.5) to assess contextual plausibility and factual accuracy. DeepSeek R-1
achieved 90.4 % accuracy and 0.93 F1, outperforming LipFD (51.24 %). The work emphasizes multimodal
verification over lip-sync cues for realistic social-media deepfake detection

positive_applications: N/A

sota_baselines:
SpotFake+ – The base architecture for all three task-specific neural networks
(Text-Only, Multimodal, and LSTM Multimodal). It combines textual features (BERT)
and visual features (VGG19) for fake news detection

VILA (NVILA 8B) – A Vision-Language Model (VLM) used in zero-shot and
Chain-of-Thought prompting to classify disinformation by jointly analyzing text and images

LLaMA 3.2 Vision (11B) – A Large Vision-Language Model (LVLM) evaluated
for unified detection across text, images, and video frames
summary:
The paper proposes a unified disinformation detection pipeline capable of jointly analyzing text, images, and videos.
Video audio is transcribed using Whisper, and three keyframe extraction methods—random sampling, K-Means clustering,
and a novel similarity-based alignment via Binary Integer Programming—create visual representations aligned with text segments.
Text is embedded with BERT, images with VGG19, and optional captions generated via BLIP2.
These modalities are combined with FakeNewsNet’s image–text pairs to build a unified multimodal dataset.
Two VLMs (LLaMA, VILA) and three neural-network architectures (text-only, multimodal, LSTM multimodal) are evaluated.
The multimodal neural network achieves the strongest overall performance, outperforming VLMs,
and similarity-based keyframes provide the most benefit in unified settings.

title: GS2F: Multimodal Fake News Detection Utilizing Graph Structure and Guided Semantic Fusion
positive_applications:
Fake news detection on social media
Improving reliability of online content classification
ethical_concerns:
Misuse of multimodal generative models for spreading misinformation;
potential data misuse from social platforms
robustness:
High generalization through contrastive learning and multimodal graph structures;
validated across 2-, 3-, and 6-class tasks on Fakeddit
data_collection: Data from Reddit (Fakeddit dataset); image–text pairs filtered to include only posts containing both modalities
detection_models: Graph Neural Networks, BERT, Swin Transformer, BiGRU, MLP
feature_extraction:
BERT for text embedding,
Faster R-CNN and Swin Transformer for image features,
DCT for frequency-domain image features
sota_baselines: Compared with MCAN, BTIC, TRIMOON, BLIP, CLIP, LIIRM, MTTV, CBAN, ITIN
summary:
GS2F introduces a graph-structured multimodal fusion framework for fake news detection.
It builds three graphs (text, image, multimodal) to capture intra- and inter-modal relationships, employs graph contrastive learning for alignment,
and integrates a guided semantic fusion module that enriches single-modal representations with external knowledge (TAGME, Wikipedia).
The model dynamically assigns feature weights via a contribution assignment layer before final classification using MLP and softmax.
It achieves superior performance across multiple Fakeddit class configurations.

positive_applications:

ethical_concerns:

Strong audio-visual deepfake detector

Multimodal contrastive learning deepfake detector
summary:
The paper introduces MACB-DF, a deep multimodal audio–video deepfake detection framework designed to address modality imbalance
and cross-modal conflicts. It extracts hierarchical multi-scale video features using the MSTLKA block and audio features using
modality-specific encoders, then applies contrastive learning to align and balance intra-modal and cross-modal representations.
A multi-head attention module fuses audio and video features, while an orthogonalization multimodal Pareto module resolves gradient
conflicts between modalities. Experiments on four deepfake datasets (DefakeAVMiT, FakeAVCeleb, DFDC, LAV-DF) using ACC and AUC
show that MACB-DF achieves up to 97.9% ACC and 98.8% AUC, and significantly outperforms state-of-the-art detectors with
strong cross-dataset generalization.

summary:
X3A is a multimodal deepfake detection framework that fuses two powerful unimodal models: X3D for video
(capturing spatio-temporal features from uniformly sampled raw frames) and AASIST for audio
(extracting deep representations directly from raw waveforms). After obtaining a fake probability score from each modality,
X3A applies probabilistic OR score-level fusion, enabling the system to classify a video as fake even if only
one modality shows evidence of manipulation. This design avoids hand-crafted features and complex alignment across modalities.
Experiments conducted on FakeAVCeleb, AV-Deepfake1M, and LAV-DF demonstrate that X3A robustly
detects both fully and partially manipulated deepfakes, achieving state-of-the-art performance,
including AUC 0.9999 and Acc 0.9960 on the AV-Deepfake1M dataset.

summary:
The paper proposes a Potential Features Fusion Network (PFFN) for multimodal fake news detection that jointly models explicit
and potential features from text and images. Explicit text features are extracted using pretrained BERT followed by Text-CNN, while explicit
image features are obtained using ResNet50. Potential text features are derived from emotion extraction, and potential image features are
modeled through manually defined image categories. A Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) structure uses image category probabilities as gating weights to
process image features, while an attention mechanism fuses emotion features with text features. Cross-attention is then applied to integrate text
and image representations for final classification. Experiments on Weibo16, Weibo19, X, and PolitiFact datasets demonstrate that PFFN
consistently outperforms single-modal and multimodal baselines across accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score.

summary:
The paper proposes MFSVFND, a multimodal fusion network for detecting fake news on short video platforms using textual, visual, and audio
content. Textual features are extracted by concatenating video transcripts and titles and encoding them with BERT, visual features are obtained
from keyframes using a pretrained MAE model, and audio features are extracted with HuBERT. The model first applies modality-specific
self-attention using stacked Transformer layers with causal and standard attention to capture intra-modality dependencies. A bidirectional
cross-modal attention module is then used to model interactions between text–visual, visual–text, and visual–audio modalities. The fused
multimodal representation is classified using a cross-entropy loss. Experiments on FakeSV and FakeTT datasets demonstrate that MFSVFND
consistently outperforms all evaluated (M)LLM-based and neural network baselines in accuracy and macro F1-score, validating the effectiveness
of deep multimodal fusion for fake news video detection.

summary:
The paper proposes ECC-FND, an emotion-enhanced cross-modal contrastive learning framework for multimodal fake news detection using
images, text, and user comments. Visual features are extracted using a pretrained ResNet model, textual features are encoded with BERT, and
emotional features are derived from both news text and user comments using sentiment analysis. The model employs cross-modal contrastive

weights modality contributions before classification. Experiments on the Weibo dataset demonstrate that ECC-FND outperforms all evaluated
state-of-the-art baselines in accuracy and F1-score, validating the effectiveness of emotion-aware contrastive learning for fake news detection.

summary:
This paper proposes EARAM, a rationale-augmented multimodal fake news detection framework that combines the reasoning strengths of Large
Vision-Language Models with the task-specific classification abilities of Multimodal Small Language Models. LVLMs are first used, with
retrieval-augmented prompting, to generate multi-perspective analyses of news content based on common-sense reasoning and image-text
complementarity logic. These analyses are then encoded and selectively filtered by MSLMs through attention-based rationale extraction modules,
which integrate useful evidence while suppressing noise. The final prediction is made using fused multimodal representations, and the extracted
rationales are fed back into LVLMs to generate reliable and human-interpretable explanations. Extensive experiments show that EARAM achieves
state-of-the-art detection accuracy, improved cross-dataset generalization, and superior explanation quality compared to existing multimodal fake
news detection models.

title: Comprehensive Out-of-context Misinformation Detection via Global Information Enhancement

threaten social stability.

- Caption semantics may involve multiple objects not handled by prior models.

- Unimodal NLI models introduce bias.

- OFA_Large for MNLI

- Visual-semantic reasoning model

summary:
The paper introduces a multi-step global-information-enhanced framework for detecting cheapfake out-of-context misinformation
in (Image, Caption1, Caption2) triples. First, visual-semantic reasoning and VSRN are used to learn global image–caption alignments.
The detection pipeline begins with a Fake Statement Check, where SBERT-based probe comparisons identify contradictions or misleading
words between captions. If unresolved, the sample enters a Multimodal Natural Language Inference (MNLI) component using OFA_Large,
which predicts entailment/contradiction/neutral relationships between the image and captions in both directions. Neutral samples then go
through image-text matching and semantic comparison, combining fine-tuned VSRN retrieval scores and SBERT-WK caption similarity. Final
classification into OOC/NOOC uses threshold-based rules. The method achieves improved accuracy, recall, and F1-score over COSMOS
and multiple improved baselines on COSMOS_test and GCDC_test.

summary:
The paper proposes LLaVA-SNIPPER, a multimodal detection framework that integrates structured scene graphs with a multimodal large
language model to detect out-of-context misinformation. Object detection using Grounding DINO and relationship inference via EGTR are used
to construct scene graphs encoding fine-grained visual semantics. These structured representations are fused with visual and textual embeddings
in LLaVA and refined through an iterative online assistance mechanism and negative choice queries. The model jointly produces a classification
decision and a chain-of-thought explanation, enabling accurate and interpretable detection of semantic inconsistencies between images and
accompanying text.

summary:
The paper proposes GAMED, a novel multimodal fake news detection framework that departs from traditional fusion-centric approaches by
explicitly decoupling modalities and refining their contributions through a knowledge-adaptive mixture-of-experts architecture. Text and image
features are extracted independently using ERNIE 2.0 and Inception-ResNet/MAE-ViT, refined through expert networks, and adaptively
reweighted using an AdaIN-based distribution adjustment mechanism. A novel veto-based decision strategy dynamically manages modality
contributions to improve robustness and interpretability. Extensive experiments on Fakeddit and Yang datasets demonstrate that GAMED
achieves state-of-the-art accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 scores, while offering improved explainability and robustness over existing
multimodal fake news detection methods.

The paper proposes COOLANT, a cross-modal contrastive learning framework for multimodal fake news detection. The model uses a
dual-encoder architecture with ResNet for visual encoding and BERT for textual encoding to extract unimodal embeddings. An image-text

title: MMSFD: Multi-grained and Multi-modal Fusion for Short Video Fake News Detection

These features are processed through intermodal and intramodal attention modules to capture complex relationships within and between different data types. Finally, the model fuses these representations through weighted aggregation and average pooling to perform binary classification (real vs. fake). Experimental results on the FakeNewsNet dataset show that MSFF outperforms several state-of-the-art models, particularly in recall and accuracy

title: MSFF: A Novel Multi-Modal Semantic Feature Fusion for Social Media Fake News Detection
positive_applications: Detection: cyberspace security; social stability; election integrity; misinformation control on social media
ethical_concerns: National security threats; social instability; public deception; economic losses due to fake media

Text and image representations are aligned through semantic consistency mapping and fused using inter-modal and intra-modal attention mechanisms. The original unimodal features and fused joint representation are re-combined via attention and classified using a fully connected layer with softmax. The model is evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1, outperforming BERT, EANN, MVAE, and MSCD, with recall improved by up to 5.6% on PolitiFact and accuracy improved by 2.6% on GossipCop.

title: Multi-modal Chinese Fake News Detection
positive_applications: Detection: preserving public trust; maintaining social stability; rapid debunking of rumors; misinformation control during crises (health, politics, disasters)

To bridge the gap between modalities, the model employs image-text alignment learning and contrastive learning to map both types of data into a shared semantic space. A hybrid expert system consisting of multiple Text-CNNs and a gating mechanism is used to capture domain-specific textual characteristics , while a cross-attention mechanism identifies deep relationships and relevant visual elements based on the text. The final representation is fused and passed through an MLP for binary classification , demonstrating superior performance on the mWeibo dataset compared to single-modal benchmarks.

title: Multimodal Cognitive Learning for Media Forgery Detection: A Comprehensive Framework Combining Random Forest and Deep Ensemble Architectures (Xception, ResNeXt) across Image, Video, and Audio Modalities
positive_applications: Detection: protect information security, protect digital media integrity, and protect against misinformation.
ethical_concerns: Misinformation campaigns; identity theft; media credibility loss;

Temporal consistency in videos is analyzed using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, while audio authenticity is verified by converting signals into Mel spectrograms and processing them through Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). All three detection streams are integrated through an ensemble fusion module that leverages the combined predictions to increase overall detection accuracy and robustness against sophisticated multi-modal forgery attacks.

title: Multimodal Fake News Analysis Based on Image–Text Similarity

ethical_concerns: Spreading false information; Misinformation has confused people in the health domain, swayed public thoughts, and influenced human behaviors and judgments
detection_limitations: The results are often difficult to interpret, particularly when visual information is included in the pipeline; need to explore the mathematical intuition behind post-training features.

Fusion: Calculations for four similarities- Textual (cosine similarity between text and caption), Semantic (cosine similarity between text and enhanced caption), Contextual (Jaccard similarity on named entities), and Post-training (cosine similarity of ViLBERT hidden representations).

summary: This paper proposes a multimodal analysis framework based on four distinct types of image-text similarity—textual, semantic, contextual, and post-training—to improve fake news detection. The methodology utilizes ResNet101 and an LSTM with attention to generate image captions, which are then "enhanced" by crawling Google Image Search to extract real-world named entities. These entities allow for contextual similarity mapping using Jaccard measurements across categories like person, location, and date. For final classification, the ViLBERT model integrates textual tokens and visual regional features through co-attention transformer layers, allowing the system to learn cross-modal interactions that evolve during training. Experimental results across three datasets demonstrate that this multimodal approach significantly outperforms single-modal benchmarks.

title: Multimodal Fake News Detection Based on Contrastive Learning and Cross-Attention Mechanism
positive_applications: Detection: misinformation mitigation on social media; protecting public trust; protect public comprehension and domains like politics and the economy.
ethical_concerns: manipulation of public opinion; disruption to politics and economy; erosion of information authenticity;
detection_limitations: Currently only considers text and image modalities; ignores news comments, background publication context, and video. Generalization issues due to small-scale datasets. Vulnerability to adversarial attacks where creators intentionally modify content to evade detection.

summary: The MMCC model is a multimodal deep learning framework designed to detect fake news by addressing feature fusion and semantic alignment challenges. The methodology utilizes BERT for textual encoding and Vision Transformer (ViT) for image feature extraction. To ensure the disparate modalities are semantically coherent, the authors implement a multimodal feature alignment module using two contrastive learning strategies: one generating image captions via CLIPCap and another using CLIP as a teacher model to guide feature mapping. These aligned features are then integrated through a cross-attention mechanism, where textual queries attend to specific image regions to identify emotional or semantic inconsistencies. Finally, the fused representations are processed through a linear layer for binary classification, achieving significant F1 score improvements over existing SOTA models like EANN and JAM across Twitter and Weibo datasets.

title: Multimodal Fake News Detection Technology Based on Deep Learning
positive_applications: Detection: prevent social crises, protect public perception

summary: The VAEMTL model is a multimodal fake news detection framework that integrates a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) with Multi-Task Learning to ensure feature effectiveness. Unlike traditional methods that simply splice features, VAEMTL uses an inference network to encode text and images into a shared hidden variable space, capturing potential cross-modal correlations. A generative decoder then reconstructs the input data from these hidden variables, a process that validates whether the extracted features are truly representative of the news content. To optimize performance, the model employs a Grad Norm strategy to dynamically allocate weights between the detection task, the reconstruction task, and a domain adversarial module. This joint training approach allows the model to balance different learning objectives, resulting in improved accuracy and generalization on both Weibo and Twitter datasets compared to existing models like MVAE and EANN.

title: Multimodal Multi-image Fake News Detection

The methodology utilizes BERT-Base to capture the contextual meaning of the news text. For visual analysis, it extracts image tags from multiple images using VGG-16 and processes them as a temporal sequence through an LSTM layer and mean pooling. A semantic component calculates the cosine similarity between Word2Vec embeddings of the article title and the image tags to detect content mismatches. These representations are concatenated and fused using an attention mechanism before a final Multi-layer Perceptron (MLP) predicts the article's authenticity. The model demonstrates that utilizing features from multiple images is more effective than single-image approaches, significantly outperforming baselines like SpotFake.

title: Multimodaltrace: Deepfake Detection using Audiovisual Representation Learning

ethical_concerns: protect personal privacy, public security against social concerns caused by realistic deepfakes
detection_limitations: performance was relatively lower on the AFVR (Fake Audio, Real Video) class compared to others. Future work: to test robustness against noise perturbations and laundering scenarios.

The methodology involves extracting spectral audio features via ResNet-1D and spatiotemporal visual features via ResNet-3D, which are then processed independently through IntrAmodality Mixer Layers (IAML). These modalities are fused and jointly analyzed in IntErModality Mixer Layers (IEML) to capture cross-modal inconsistencies. Unlike traditional binary classifiers, this model utilizes a multi-label classification head to provide simultaneous confidence scores for both audio and video authenticity, achieving a state-of-the-art accuracy of 92.9% on the FakeAVCeleb dataset.

title: PVASS-MDD: Predictive Visual-Audio Alignment Self-Supervision for Multimodal Deepfake Detection
positive_applications: Detection: protect personal privacy and public security against social concerns caused by realistic deepfakes.

summary: The PVASS-MDD framework is a two-stage multimodal detection system designed to capture subtle visual-audio (VA) inconsistencies, especially in videos with collaborative forgeries. The methodology begins with the PVASS auxiliary stage, where a three-stream network uses two augmented visual views and a novel Predictive VA Alignment (PVA) module to bridge the modality gap by iteratively predicting audio features from visual priors. The second stage, MDD, utilizes the frozen PVASS network to provide alignment targets for real videos through an auxiliary loss, helping the detector (built on Swin-Transformer and VGGish) better distinguish subtle discrepancies in fake videos. By training with a combination of cross-entropy, contrastive, and auxiliary losses, the model achieves state-of-the-art performance, recording an average accuracy of 96.5% across multiple benchmark datasets

title: SpotFake: A Multi-modal Framework for Fake News Detection

The methodology utilizes a pre-trained BERT-Base model to extract deep contextual textual features and a pre-trained VGG-19 network to capture visual representations from news images. These features are reduced in dimensionality via fully connected layers and fused through a simple concatenation technique to form a unified news representation vector. This vector is then processed by a fully connected classifier to distinguish between real and fake content. Evaluated on the Twitter and Weibo datasets, SpotFake outperformed existing state-of-the-art models, achieving significant accuracy gains by prioritizing the primary detection task.

title: Tri-FusionDet: Leveraging User Engagement, Textual, and Visual Features for Enhanced Fake News Detection

summary: Tri-FusionDet is a multimodal fake news detection framework designed to address the challenges posed by generative AI and social media misinformation. The methodology utilizes a late fusion approach to independently process three distinct data streams: textual features extracted via a fine-tuned DistilBERT model, visual features processed through a retrained ResNet18 architecture, and social engagement metrics (comments, upvote ratio, and score). By combining these modalities into a final XGBoost classifier, the system achieves a 94% accuracy on the Fakeddit dataset, outperforming early-fusion models like SpotFake and MVAE. The research emphasizes the critical role of social context in improving detection accuracy while identifying model explainability and the inclusion of additional modalities like audio as key areas for future development.

The methodology introduces Multi-modal Circulant Fusion (MCF), which employs circulant matrices to capture complex interactions between text and images more effectively than simple splicing while maintaining computational efficiency. To improve generalization for emerging events, the model incorporates an adversarial domain classifier that removes event-specific features. Evaluated on Twitter and Weibo datasets, ALB-MCF demonstrates superior performance over existing SOTA techniques like BDANN and MVAE, highlighting the effectiveness of its specialized fusion and extraction modules in identifying deceptive multimedia content.

title: An Explainable Multi-view Semantic Fusion Model for Multimodal Fake News Detection

The methodology employs a Modal Alignment Module to translate images into natural language descriptions, bridging the semantic gap. It utilizes a Shared Semantic Space to identify representative high-frequency words in fake news and a Multi-view Semantic Fusion Module that decomposes multimodal inputs into consistent and inconsistent representations. Specialized "semantic experts" evaluate these views to calculate a joint credibility score. Experiments on the Fakeddit and Weibo datasets show that EMSFM outperforms state-of-the-art models like MCAN and Spotfake+ while providing an explainable perspective on how multimodal inconsistencies contribute to the classification of fake news.

ethical_concerns: Misleading readers, inciting social media users to believe and disseminate inaccurate information, and potentially causing political unrest, social disruption, or economic loss

summary: The paper proposes TieFake, a multimodal fake news detection framework that integrates textual, visual, emotional, and semantic relationship features to improve fake news detection on social media. The system uses BERT to extract textual representations and ResNeSt-50 to obtain visual features from news images. To capture psychological signals of misinformation, the model also extracts author subjective emotion features using a publisher emotion extractor. Additionally, the model introduces a scaled dot-product attention mechanism to compute the semantic similarity between the news title and article text, capturing misleading headline patterns common in fake news. These representations are fused into a unified 164-dimensional multimodal feature vector, which is passed to a fully connected classifier to predict whether a news article is fake or real. Experiments conducted on the PolitiFact and GossipCop datasets from FakeNewsNet demonstrate that the proposed TieFake model outperforms existing text-based, image-based, and multimodal fake news detection baselines.

title: A bi-level multi-modal fake generative news detection approach: from the perspective of emotional manipulation purpose
positive_applications: Detection: Improving cyberspace security, detecting AI-generated misinformation Protecting social, political, and economic stability; Generation: Simulating crowd emotions to eliminate regional or cultural biases in comment analysis.
ethical_concerns: Threatening Internet security, escalating regional and national tensions, and manipulating public emotions to incite protests or unrest.

summary: This paper proposes EmoDect, a bi-level multimodal fake AIGC detection framework designed to identify AI-generated fake news based on emotional manipulation patterns. Unlike traditional detection methods that focus on semantic inconsistencies between modalities, EmoDect analyzes emotional signals at two levels: the publisher level (news content) and the reviewer level (comments). The model first extracts emotional representations from text, audio, and video modalities using Bi-LSTM, Transformer-based audio encoders, and Vision Transformer-based visual encoders. It then generates modality-specific comments using large language models to simulate crowd emotional responses. The framework learns multiple emotional consistency relationships, including cross-modal post consistency, comment-level emotional fluctuation, publisher–reviewer emotional alignment, and second-order consistency across modalities. These signals are integrated using a multi-loss training strategy to classify news as fake or real. Experiments on Twitter and FaceFake datasets show that EmoDect outperforms several baseline models by leveraging multimodal emotional inconsistencies for detecting fake AI-generated content.

title: AMPLE: Emotion-Aware Multimodal Fusion Prompt Learning for Fake News Detection
positive_applications: Detection: Helping social media platforms identify misinformation with limited data (few-shot learning), reducing the reliance on massive annotated datasets
ethical_concerns: creating economic and political risks, spreading misinformation on social networks.

summary: The paper proposes AMPLE, an emotion-aware multimodal fake news detection framework that integrates textual and visual information with sentiment-aware prompt learning. The system uses a pre-trained CLIP model to extract unified text and image features while employing a sentiment analysis tool (SAT) to capture emotional elements such as polarity and subjectivity from textual content. These emotional signals are combined with multimodal representations using a Multi-head Cross-Attention (MCA) mechanism that enables deep interaction between text and image features. A hybrid prompt-learning approach based on RoBERTa-base introduces both fixed and trainable prompt tokens to improve performance in few-shot learning scenarios, where labeled data is limited. The fused multimodal representation is then used for fake news classification. Experiments conducted on the PolitiFact and GossipCop datasets demonstrate that AMPLE consistently outperforms several unimodal and multimodal baseline methods in terms of macro F1-score and accuracy, highlighting the effectiveness of incorporating emotional elements and prompt learning for multimodal fake news detection.

title: AMTCF: an advanced multimodal transformer and ConvNext fusion for contextualized fake news detection in digital landscape

summary: he AMTCF framework introduces a contextualized approach to fake news detection by integrating textual, visual, and thematic information. The methodology utilizes DistilBERT to generate text embeddings, which are then compressed using a beta-Variational Autoencoder to optimize efficiency while retaining critical information. Simultaneously, ConvNeXt-Tiny extracts high-level visual features from images preprocessed with CLAHE. A unique contribution is the use of the Pachinko Allocation Model (PAM), which employs Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) structures to perform thematic analysis, capturing deeper subject-level context. These three distinct feature sets—semantic, visual, and thematic—are integrated via a late fusion strategy and classified by a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), providing a robust solution tailored for the complex digital landscape, particularly within the Indian context.

summary: The paper proposes MANN (Mutual Attention Neural Network), a multimodal fake news detection framework that analyzes both textual content and associated images from social media posts. The model first extracts textual features using word embeddings and Bi-LSTM networks, while visual features are extracted using CNN architectures such as VGG-16 or VGG-19. A novel bi-directional mutual attention mechanism is introduced to model the interaction between text and image modalities, allowing each modality to attend to the other. The fused multimodal representation is then passed to a fake news classifier and an event discriminator to remove event-specific biases and improve generalization across new events. Experiments conducted on Weibo and Twitter datasets demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms existing multimodal fake news detection approaches such as EANN and att-RNN.

Text and image features are extracted separately using the pre-trained models, normalized to a unified vector space, and then concatenated to form multimodal feature representations. These fused features are passed through fully connected layers and a softmax classifier to determine whether a news item is fake or real. The model is evaluated on three Chinese fake news datasets including epidemic-related news data and multimodal fake news benchmarks. Experimental results demonstrate that the Albert-ResNet50 multimodal framework outperforms traditional text-based models such as TextCNN and Bi-LSTM, showing that combining textual and visual information improves fake news detection performance.

A unique component is the extraction of multimodal emotions: visual emotions are processed via a fine-tuned VGG-16, and textual emotions are quantified using the NRC emotion lexicon and Wikipedia emoticon data. These features are integrated through concatenation, allowing the model to analyze the alignment and emotional resonance between modalities. Final classification is performed by a Softmax classifier, which outperformed several state-of-the-art benchmarks across five diverse datasets including Twitter and Reddit.

Simultaneously, it employs a Capsule Neural Network (CapsNet) to extract informative visual features, utilizing a routing-by-agreement algorithm to preserve spatial hierarchies and avoid the information loss typical of CNN pooling layers. These extracted features from both modalities are concatenated into a unified 32-dimensional feature vector. This fused representation is finally processed through a fully connected layer with a softmax activation function to classify the news as fake or real.

The methodology begins by utilizing BERT for text encoding and Vision GNN to represent images as graph-structured data, which allows the model to capture relationships between complex objects while ignoring irrelevant backgrounds. To align these modalities, the framework employs Consistency Contrastive Learning, using an instance-level contrastive loss to minimize the semantic distance between corresponding text and image features. Finally, a cross-attention mechanism interactively fuses the refined features, allowing the model to select key image regions based on textual sequences for accurate binary classification. Experimental results on Weibo and Twitter benchmarks demonstrate its superiority, achieving improved accuracy and an AUC of up to 0.95

title: Clip-GCN: an adaptive detection model for multimodal emergent fake news domains

These features are processed through a Domain-Adversarial Neural Network to filter out domain-specific attributes and capture domain-invariant features. Simultaneously, a Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) is utilized to construct relational networks within specific news domains, treating news articles as nodes and establishing edges based on cosine similarity to leverage domain-specific knowledge. The final fused and refined features are fed into a label predictor for binary authenticity classification, achieving an average accuracy of 88.7% across major social media benchmarks.

summary: The ILMF-FND (Improved Low-rank Multimodal Fusion for Fake News Detection) is an end-to-end deep learning framework designed to efficiently detect multimodal fake news while minimizing model parameters. The methodology begins with extracting text features via BERT and image features via ResNet-34, which are then refined through a Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts (MMOE) network to bridge the semantic gap between modalities. A contrastive learning auxiliary task is employed to align text-image pairs in a shared semantic space. For fusion, the model uses LSTM for temporal compression followed by Improved Low-rank Multimodal Fusion (ILMF), which utilizes tensor decomposition to reduce computational complexity. Finally, a Model Adaption Module quantifies "modal fitness" using KL divergence to adaptively assign weights to unimodal and multimodal features before classification.

summary: The Coupled ConvNet is a hybrid two-stream convolutional architecture designed for multi-modal fake news detection through late fusion of textual and visual data. The methodology utilizes a Text-CNN module that processes news titles and text via Glove embeddings and 1-D convolutions to extract latent linguistic features. Simultaneously, an Image-CNN module leverages fine-tuned pre-trained models such as VGG16 or Xception to identify latent visual patterns in news images. After individual training of these streams, their output prediction probabilities are combined using a weighted average late fusion technique, where specific weights are assigned to each modality to optimize final classification accuracy. This framework effectively classifies news as real or fake by analyzing both the written claims and the authenticity of accompanying visual content.

summary: The DMVAE (Dual-Stream Multi-modal Variational Autoencoder) is an advanced Encoder-Decoder framework designed for multi-task fake news detection. The Encoder utilizes a dual-stream network to extract both deep and shallow features: BERT and Text-CNN for sentence and word-level text features, and ResNet-50 for global and regional image features. To enrich these representations, it applies Self-Attention for intra-modal enhancement and Multimodal Compact Bilinear Pooling (MCB) for efficient inter-modal interaction. The resulting fused features are parameterized through a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) structure to learn a shared distribution. The Decoder concurrently performs three tasks: Feature Reconstruction to verify feature validity, a Domain Discriminator to remove event-specific biases via adversarial training, and a Fake Predictor for final classification. A multi-task loss function with dynamic weight assignment is used to balance these objectives and improve overall generalization.

summary: The proposed methodology employs a multimodal deep learning framework that leverages both textual and visual information for robust fake information detection. It utilizes a pre-trained Bert model followed by a two-layer LSTM to extract deep textual semantics, while a pre-trained VGG-19 model captures visual features from images. Unlike traditional methods that rely on simple feature concatenation, this model introduces a Double MCBP (Multimodal Compact Bilinear Pooling) architecture. summary: The SMFN (Semantic-enhanced Multimodal Fusion Network) is an end-to-end framework designed to identify fake news by capturing deep mutual features between textual and visual data. The methodology utilizes three specialized extractors: VGG-19 for visual features, Text-CNN for word-level statistical embeddings, and BERT for high-level semantic extraction. summary: The paper proposes ART-AVDF, a multimodal deepfake detection framework that incorporates articulatory representations to model physiological correlations between speech production and lip movement. summary: The paper proposes a novel Uncertainty-aware Disentangled Representation Learning (UDRL) framework for multimodal fake news detection. Modality Synaptic Scaling (MSS) dynamically controls the contribution of the audio and visual representations so that modality-specific forgery cues are preserved. DDL-AV: 26 video + 9 audio forgery methods; GAN, diffusion and VAE-based generation; face swapping, reenactment, synthesis, editing, TTS/voice manipulation, deletion/insertion; includes AIGC video such as Kling-2.1
detection_models: ERF-BA-TFD+
sota_baselines: BMN; BMN-E2E; MDS; AGT; BSN++; AVFusion; BA-TFD; TadTR; ActionFormer; TriDet
summary: ERF-BA-TFD+ jointly processes visual and audio streams for deepfake detection and temporal localization. Visual representations are extracted using MViTv2, while audio representations are obtained with BYOL-A. The Cross-Reconstruction Attention Transformer (CRATrans) reconstructs one modality using the other, so cross-modal temporal inconsistencies produce high reconstruction errors. Separate frame-level classifiers detect modality-specific manipulation, followed by boundary localization based on a BSN++-inspired Proposal Relation Block. UMMA balances audio-video fusion, particularly for single-modality attacks, while the ERF module globally re-evaluates videos to detect full-length forgeries that lack clear temporal boundaries.

title: Multi-modal Deepfake Detection: A Hybrid Approach Utilizing Video, Audio, and Textual Features
positive_applications: social-media content verification; digital-media forensics; protection against manipulated audiovisual content; real-world deepfake monitoring
ethical_concerns: Misinformation; privacy violations; impersonation; fraudulent content; manipulated speech/video
detection_limitations:
Dataset imbalance across DFDC, FakeAVCeleb, and FaceForensics++; limited diversity and possible overfitting to known manipulation patterns; real-world generalization remains challenging.
Future work: random sampling/undersampling/focal loss, better data quality and diversity, balanced datasets, stronger regularization, transfer learning, improved fusion, and additional facial/behavioral modalities.
robustness:
1) Tri-modal Video + Audio + Text fusion provides complementary evidence when one modality alone misses manipulation cues.
2) Data augmentation, class reweighting, L2 regularization, dropout/early stopping, and multi-dataset evaluation are used to reduce overfitting and improve robustness
data_collection:
DFDC: public Facebook deepfake dataset with >100,000 videos.
FakeAVCeleb: public multimodal deepfake dataset with about 22,000 videos containing facial/audio/textual modifications.
FaceForensics++: public manipulated-video benchmark; this paper mentions DeepFakes, Face2Face, and FaceSwap. Authors do not create a new dataset.
detection_models: Hybrid 3D-CNN + GRU multimodal classifier
feature_extraction:
Video: ResNet50 preprocessing/features
Audio: Mel-spectrogram
Text: Whisper ASR
 Fusion: feature concatenation
sota_baselines: MesoNet; Emotions Don’t Lie; XceptionNet (VGG-19)
summary: The proposed hybrid multimodal model processes video, audio, and text in parallel. Video frames are preprocessed using ResNet50-based extraction and modeled using 3D-CNN layers to capture spatial-temporal manipulation cues. Audio is extracted from the video, converted into Mel-spectrogram representations, and processed using stacked GRUs. Audio is also transcribed using OpenAI Whisper; the resulting text is tokenized, embedded, and modeled using GRUs to capture linguistic inconsistencies. The three learned modality representations are then concatenated in a shared fusion layer, refined through dense layers with ReLU activation, and passed to a sigmoid classifier for real/fake prediction

title: MC-AVD: Generalizable Audio-Visual Deepfake Detection via Multi-modal Collaboration
positive_applications: Audiovisual authenticity verification; social-media content moderation; deepfake screening; multimedia forensics; detection of unseen forgery techniques
ethical_concerns: Impersonation; forged audiovisual statements; misinformation; manipulation of public figures; erosion of media credibility and social trust
detection_limitations: Current evaluation is primarily based on FakeAVCeleb; computational cost remains a deployment concern; broader validation across datasets and emerging manipulation types is still needed
robustness:
1) Q-Former-based cross-modal semantic alignment projects frozen visual/audio representations into a shared semantic space, improving comparability across modalities and unseen attacks.
2) Joint Transformer audiovisual fusion + modality/cross-modal regularization learns fine-grained semantic interactions rather than relying on modality-specific artifacts.
data_collection: FakeAVCeleb: public dataset containing 500 authentic and 19,500 manipulated videos. Authors use balanced intra-dataset evaluation and a cross-manipulation protocol where one manipulation type is excluded during training and used for testing. Manipulations include SV2TTS, Wav2Lip, FaceSwap, and FSGAN. No new dataset created by the authors.
detection_models: MC-AVD
sota_baselines: VFD; AVoiD-DF; AVFakeNet; AVDF; Multimodaltrace; MRDF-CE
summary: MC-AVD first extracts visual representations using a frozen CLIP-ViT-L/14 encoder and audio representations using a frozen BEATs encoder. Because the two pretrained encoders produce heterogeneous modality-specific representations, separate Q-Former modules use learnable query tokens and cross-attention to project both streams into a shared semantic space. The aligned audio and visual token sequences are then concatenated and processed jointly by a multi-layer Transformer encoder, allowing self-attention to model intra-modal dependencies and fine-grained cross-modal interactions. The pooled audiovisual representation is passed to a classifier. Training additionally uses cross-entropy together with modality and cross-modal regularization losses to reduce overfitting to modality-specific artifacts and improve generalization to unseen manipulation types.

title: Truth be told: a multimodal ensemble approach for enhanced fake news detection in textual and visual media
positive_applications: multimodal news credibility verification
ethical_concerns: socio-political harm
detection_limitations:
The framework currently uses mainly text and image content and does not incorporate user/social metadata. Dataset availability with rich text, visual, profile, and metadata information is limited. Weibo translation from Chinese to English is also imperfect.
Future work: incorporate user metadata, construct larger multimodal benchmark datasets, investigate POS tagging/topic modeling, and explore semi-supervised, unsupervised, hybrid, information-retrieval, and reinforcement-learning approaches.
robustness:
1) Ensembles SBERT and DeBERT textual representations to reduce dependence on a single language model.
2) Uses Gaussian-noise image augmentation and evaluates across two different-language/platform datasets (Twitter and Weibo), supporting robustness to limited visual data and dataset variation
data_collection:
Twitter/MediaEval: Real-world text-image posts; fake cases include an image unrelated to the event described by the tweet; no synthetic GAN/LLM generator reported.
Weibo: Real-world Sina Weibo rumors verified through Weibo’s official rumor-debunking mechanism; contains text + photos/GIFs; no synthetic generator reported
detection_models: multimodal stacked ensemble framework
sota_baselines: SpotFake; Cultural Algorithm; RoBERTa Model; SCTI; SCATE; VERITE; BDANN; EANN; MVAE; SEMI-FND
summary: The proposed framework extracts textual representations using SBERT and DeBERT and visual representations using pretrained ResNet-50. Image features are further projected through fully connected layers and a Transformer. The text and image embeddings are joined to form a multimodal representation and processed using multi-head self-attention. In parallel, the framework employs an ensemble strategy using soft/hard voting and equal-weight averaging to combine predictions from the constituent models before performing binary real/fake classification.

title: Multi-domain feature enhanced adaptive fusion network for multi-modal fake news detection
positive_applications: credibility verification
ethical_concerns: spread misinformation
detection_limitations: No explicit future-work section is provided. Evaluation uses only Weibo and PHEME, and samples missing either text or image are removed, so robustness to missing modalities is not evaluated
robustness:
1) CLIP shared-domain representations reduce the semantic gap between text and image.
2) Adaptive WeightMLP dynamically changes the importance of text-image, image-social, and text-social features for each post instead of fixed fusion, improving adaptability to diverse fake-news patterns.
data_collection:
Weibo: Real-world Chinese multimodal news authenticated using Xinhua; text + image + user/comment information; no synthetic generator reported.
PHEME: Real-world Twitter breaking-news rumors/non-rumors containing text, images, comments and user information; no synthetic generator reported.
detection_models: MDEAF – Multi-Domain Feature Enhanced Adaptive Fusion Network
sota_baselines: EANN; SpotFake; SpotFake++; SAFE; CARMN; MFAN; CAFE
summary: MDEAF represents fake news from four complementary domains. Text semantic features are extracted using multi-scale CNNs over word embeddings, while image manipulation cues are captured by applying DCT and a CNN to image-frequency information. CLIP supplies aligned text-image representations in a shared semantic space, and a Signed GAT models users, posts and comments in the social domain. Each domain is first enhanced using multi-head self-attention. The model then performs two rounds of bidirectional multi-head cross-attention among text, visual and social representations. Finally, a WeightMLP learns sample-dependent weights for text-image, image-social and text-social interactions; the weighted features are concatenated and classified using fully connected layers.

title: A local dynamic propagation graph-based method for multi-modal fake news detection
positive_applications: propagation-aware credibility analysis
ethical_concerns: threatens public opinion and information credibility
detection_limitations:
Current temporal and cross-modal modeling can still be made more fine-grained.
 Future work: improve temporal modeling, strengthen cross-modal interaction, use larger-scale real-world propagation data, and improve robustness/scalability across diverse domains and scenarios
robustness:
1) Local dynamic propagation windows with activity-based pruning remove old/noisy interactions and retain influential nodes, improving early-stage robustness and efficiency.
2) Time-aware contrastive alignment aligns static text-image content with evolving propagation representations, reducing semantic drift over time
data_collection:
PHEME: Real-world Twitter breaking-news posts with text, images, and propagation/user interactions; no synthetic generator reported.
PolitiFact: Real-world U.S. political news from FakeNewsNet with text, images, users, and propagation information; no synthetic generator reported.
 GossipCop: Real-world celebrity/gossip news from FakeNewsNet with text, images, users, and propagation information; no synthetic generator reported.
detection_models: LDPG – Local Dynamic Propagation Graph
sota_baselines: BERT; EANN; MVAE; MCAN; IARNet; MFAN; MGIN-AG; MST; ESDGFN
summary: LDPG first encodes text using RoBERTa and images using ResNet-18. The text and image representations are projected into a shared space and fused using bidirectional multi-head attention, where image-guided text attention and text-guided image attention are computed separately; the two interacted representations are then passed through FFNs and concatenated. Next, the model builds a local dynamic propagation graph using sliding time windows and activity-based pruning to retain current, influential user interactions. A Heterogeneous GAT models the propagation structure, while a GRU captures temporal evolution across windows. Finally, contrastive alignment enforces consistency between static text-image content and dynamic propagation features, which are concatenated and passed to a Softmax classifier.

title: A unified approach for fake news detection: dynamic fusion of uni-modal and multi-modal features
positive_applications: misinformation moderation.
ethical_concerns: erode public trust, and threaten social/political stability;
detection_limitations:
UMFN requires the modalities to coexist because CLIP similarity depends on both text and image; it is vulnerable to missing-modality cases, is not designed for long-form content, and struggles with text-rich screenshots because it lacks explicit OCR/typographical extraction.
Future work: modality dropout, hierarchical fusion for long text, diffusion-based alignment for extremely weak cross-modal relationships, and OCR/LVLM integration.
robustness:
1) Independent uni-modal branches preserve text, visual and frequency-specific evidence when cross-modal correlation is weak.
2) CLIP cosine-similarity adaptive weighting dynamically shifts between multimodal fusion and uni-modal evidence, reducing decision conflict from mismatched text-image pairs and supporting out-of-domain robustness
data_collection:
Weibo: Existing real-world Chinese text-image fake-news dataset; fake content officially identified by Weibo authorities; no synthetic generator used by the authors.
Twitter/MediaEval: Existing real-world text-image multimedia-verification dataset; videos, missing-text and missing-image samples removed; no synthetic generator used by the authors
detection_models: UMFN – Uni-modal and Multi-modal Fusion Network
sota_baselines: EANN; MVAE; BDANN; SpotFake; HMCAN; MCAN; CAFE; DIFF; MPFN; CSFND; MFCAN; MEA; BSEAN
summary: UMFN uses three complementary branches. BERT-base extracts textual semantics, PVTv2 extracts visual semantics, and DCT followed by a multi-branch dilated CNN captures physical frequency-domain manipulation traces. Pairwise parameter-shared co-attention is performed for text–visual, text–frequency, and visual–frequency pairs, and the resulting interaction features are combined into a multimodal representation. In parallel, separate uni-modal branches preserve modality-specific evidence. A frozen CLIP model computes text-image cosine similarity, which dynamically controls how much weight is assigned to the multimodal representation versus the individual uni-modal branches. The weighted representations are concatenated and passed to a fully connected classifier for real/fake prediction.

title: Multimodal Consistency-Driven Deepfake Detection
positive_applications: audiovisual authenticity verification; social-media content moderation; forensic analysis
ethical_concerns: Misinformation; fabricated statements; impersonation; manipulation of public figures; erosion of media trust
detection_limitations: Mainly evaluated on FakeAVCeleb; further validation is needed for streaming video, diverse datasets, and evolving/adaptive attacks. Future work proposes streaming analysis and adaptive learning.
robustness: Cross-modal lip-speech consistency learning captures manipulation beyond unimodal artifacts; One-Class Softmax improves generalization to unseen manipulation techniques.
data_collection: FakeAVCeleb
detection_models: AVMCD
sota_baselines: AVFakeNet; VFD; AVoiD-DF; AV-DFD; AVAD-LRS2; AVAD-LRS3
summary: AVMCD extracts spatiotemporal visual features using ViViT and spectral-temporal audio features using MFCC followed by AST. Cross-modal attention models lip-speech synchronization and produces an audiovisual consistency representation. One-Class Softmax is applied to modality-specific branches, while an audiovisual consistency loss measures temporal correlation between lip movement and speech. Video, audio, and AV-consistency features are then adaptively weighted and summed, and an MLP produces the final real/fake prediction

title: Multi-modal Audiovisual Deepfake Detection Using CNN, LSTM and XGB
positive_applications: authenticity analysis.
ethical_concerns: Deepfakes can spread misinformation, manipulate audiovisual evidence, impersonate people, and create convincing fake social-media content.
detection_limitations: Current system depends on relatively narrow datasets and may struggle with diverse real-world conditions, unseen manipulation techniques, and poor-quality/compressed media.
robustness:
1) Video model combines spatial CNN features with temporal LSTM modeling, helping detect frame-level inconsistencies across time.
2) Audio detection combines CNN spectrogram modeling with XGBoost handcrafted features, providing complementary learned + statistical cues.
data_collection:
Video: Celeb-DF-V2 and YouTube data; 50% original + 50% manipulated, split 80% training / 20% validation.
Audio: public Fake-or-Real (FoR) dataset with real and fake audio samples. Exact fake-generation algorithm for the authors’ custom video set is not specified.
detection_models: Video: ResNeXt-50 + LSTM; Audio: XGBoost + CNN ensemble
datasets: Celeb-DF-V2; custom Celeb-DF-V2 + YouTube video set; Fake-or-Real (FoR) audio dataset
feature_extraction:
Video: ResNeXt-50 spatial features
 Audio: CNN on spectrograms
Fusion: decision-level combination
sota_baselines: RNN-based Deepfake Video Detection; CNN-based Deepfake Detection

title: A Multimodal Fake News Detection Method Combining Adaptive Graph Convolutional Networks
positive_applications: Social-media misinformation filtering; credibility verification; detection of complex multimodal social-media content.
ethical_concerns: Fake news can influence public opinion, social stability, public trust, politics, the economy, and public health
detection_limitations:
KAMGCN has slower detection and higher computational-resource requirements than simpler models.
Future work: improve real-time performance, reduce resource consumption, incorporate additional knowledge graphs and social dynamics, and evaluate across different languages and cultural backgrounds
robustness:
1) Adaptive GCN dynamically learns node dependencies instead of relying on a fixed heuristic graph, improving flexibility for different news structures.
2) External knowledge concepts are added to the multimodal graph, providing auxiliary semantic information beyond the raw post content
data_collection:
PHEME: Existing public social-media fake-news dataset containing text, images, and contextual information; no synthetic generator used by authors.
WEIBO: Existing public social-network dataset containing text, images, and responses/comments; no synthetic generator used by authors
detection_models: KAMGCN – Knowledge-Driven Adaptive Multimodal Graph Convolutional Network
sota_baselines: CNN; GRU; KMGCN; SpotFake
summary: KAMGCN converts each multimodal news post into a unified graph containing textual information, visual information, and external knowledge concepts. Entity linking/knowledge distillation extracts relevant knowledge concepts, while PMI establishes relationships among textual elements. Initial node representations are obtained from pretrained language embeddings. Instead of keeping a fixed graph structure, Adaptive Graph Convolutional Networks dynamically learn relationships between nodes using multi-head graph attention. Two AGCN layers aggregate information across text, image, and knowledge nodes, followed by graph pooling to obtain a post-level multimodal representation, which is then passed to a binary classifier for real/fake prediction

title: Multimodal fake news detection in Hindi using adaptive gated fusion
positive_applications: misinformation filteringmisinformation filtering
ethical_concerns: Fake content can manipulate public opinion and elections, spread fear/panic, cause financial loss or identity theft, harm reputations, spread hate, and affect public health.
detection_limitations:
Evaluated on only one Hindi dataset; cross-dataset/cross-domain generalization is not tested; random splitting may still allow source/event overlap; no temporal/source/event metadata; only text + image are considered; performance drops strongly under image–text mismatch; noisy images can also degrade performance.
 Future work: multilingual/cross-domain evaluation, event/temporal splits, audio/video modalities, stronger noisy-input robustness, and real-time deployment.
robustness:
1) Learnable modality alignment maps CLIP image features into the same space as the textual representation.
2) Sample-wise adaptive gating dynamically weights text versus image instead of using fixed fusion, allowing the model to emphasize whichever modality is more informative.
data_collection: Authors created a new Hindi multimodal dataset. News was collected from Dainik Jagran, Dainik Bhaskar, Amar Ujala, and BoomLive. Original: 29,285 records; after cleaning: 27,596 = 17,933 true + 9,663 fake. Labels were assigned using a verification script plus manual author review against fact-check reports/reliable sources. Duplicate/ambiguous items and low-quality/irrelevant images were removed. No GAN/LLM/synthetic generator was used
detection_models: GMFN – Gated Multimodal Fusion Network
sota_baselines: BERT+CNN; SpotFake+; CARMN+MCNN; CB-Fake; CNN+BERT; A-KWGCN; MBPAM; SCL-based; SSM; Contrastive Learning; Event-Radar; MFUIE; MUSE; MMHFND     Multimodal fake news detection …
summary: GMFN processes Hindi text using IndicBERT, followed by BiLSTM and attention to obtain a context-aware textual representation. Images are encoded using a frozen CLIP ViT-B/32 encoder. A feedforward modality-alignment layer projects the image representation into the same latent space as the text. The aligned text and image vectors are concatenated and passed to a learnable Softmax gating layer, which produces separate weights for the two modalities. The final multimodal representation is a weighted sum of text and image features and is passed to a fully connected classifier for real/fake prediction.

title: Fake news detection with GAN-augmented contrastive learning and multimodal attention
positive_applications: misinformation verification;
ethical_concerns: Fake news can distort public opinion, affect elections, incite unrest, reduce information credibility, and undermine public trust.
detection_limitations:
Text-CNN has difficulty modeling long-term dependencies in long text; the framework only uses text + image and excludes audio/video; the GAN uses a relatively simple discriminator that may cause generator–discriminator imbalance.
Future work: stronger text modeling such as LSTM-based approaches, more balanced/complex GAN structures, and extension to audio/video multimodal misinformation.
robustness:
1) Event-invariant adversarial learning forces the multimodal extractor to remove event-specific information, improving generalization to unseen events.
2) PGD-augmented supervised contrastive learning trains the representation against adversarial perturbations, improving attack robustness.
data_collection:
Twitter/MediaEval: existing public text-image misinformation dataset; train/test events are kept distinct and text-only/image-only samples removed; no synthetic generator used by authors.
Weibo: existing public Chinese real/fake news from Xinhua and Weibo’s rumor-refutation system; duplicate/low-quality images removed and events separated between train/test; no synthetic generator used by author
detection_models: MADSL – Multimodal Adversarial Deep Semantic Learning
sota_baselines: VQA; SAFE; att-RNN
summary: MADSL first extracts textual features using Word2Vec + Text-CNN and visual features using a pretrained VGG-19. The two modalities are fused using a multi-layer text-image co-attention mechanism, where the textual representation acts as a query over image regions; relevant visual regions are weighted and progressively added to the text representation across several attention layers. The resulting multimodal feature is then trained adversarially against an event classifier, forcing the feature extractor to learn event-invariant representations. Finally, supervised contrastive learning with PGD-generated adversarial perturbations further separates real/fake representations and improves robustness to attacks.

title: A Comprehensive Evaluation of Multimodal Fake News Detection: Assessing Robustness and Efficacy
positive_applications: Robust multimodal misinformation detection; adversarial vulnerability assessment;
ethical_concerns: undermine public trust, and increase vulnerability of automated verification systems
detection_limitations:
Strong unimodal/visual bias; text-based adversarial attacks cause major degradation; missing modalities severely affect performance; D1 contains visible “FAKE/MISLEADING/HOAX” watermarks that may create shortcut learning and inflate visual performance.
 Future work: cleaner datasets such as GossipCop/PolitiFact, dynamic fusion, adversarial defenses, cross-lingual generalization, modality-balanced learning, realistic generative-AI benchmarks, and stronger multimodal robustnes
robustness: No new robustness mechanism is proposed; instead the paper systematically evaluates robustness using 10 image attacks + 5 text attacks including LLaMA3-based attacks, and evaluates modality removal/unimodal bias. It also introduces a Synergy Gain analysis to measure whether fusion truly improves over the strongest unimodal branch.
data_collection:
D1: Existing benchmark; 4,843 samples = 2,613 fake + 2,230 real; many fake images contain visible “FAKE/MISLEADING/HOAX” watermarks.
RECOVERY: Existing COVID-19 misinformation dataset; 1,135 real + 310 fake samples; real-world misinformation related to pandemics/natural disasters.
detection_models: BERT-VGG; CNN-VGG; LSTM-VGG
sota_baselines: EANN; Att-RNN; SpotFake
summary: The study compares three multimodal architectures: BERT-VGG, CNN-VGG, and LSTM-VGG. Each uses a different text encoder—BERT, Text-CNN, or LSTM—while all use VGG-19 for visual features. Text and image representations are projected into a common latent space and fused through an additive multimodal co-attention mechanism, which computes separate attention vectors for text and image and forms a weighted multimodal representation for classification. Rather than proposing a new detector, the authors stress-test these architectures using 10 image attacks, 5 text attacks including LLaMA3-generated adversarial text, and modality-removal experiments to analyze adversarial robustness, cross-modal synergy, and unimodal bias.

title: Multimodal based Amharic fake news detection using CNN and attention-based BiLSTM
positive_applications: Amharic fake-news detection; Facebook misinformation monitoring
ethical_concerns: political manipulation, societal division, and threats to national unity.
detection_limitations:
Dataset is limited in size/scope compared with real-world social media; generalizability may therefore be limited. Text modeling can be affected by Amharic code-mixing, spelling variations, and culturally specific expressions. Current model performs only binary real/fake classification.
Future work: larger datasets, image captioning, OCR, and hierarchical classification of satire, false context, fabricated content, et
robustness:
1) Attention-based BiLSTM emphasizes informative Amharic words while modeling bidirectional context.
2) Late fusion keeps image and text classifiers independent before combination, which the authors argue is more robust to modality-specific noise.
data_collection: Authors created a new dataset of 23,856 Amharic text-image news posts collected from selected Facebook pages using Facepager + Facebook Graph API 13.0. Text and images were manually evaluated by multiple experts using news-literacy guidelines; linguistic experts checked factual/misleading text, while images were checked for manipulation, contextual relevance, and text-image consistency. Disagreements were resolved by consensus. No synthetic generator was used
metrics: Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-score, confusion matrix;
detection_models: CNN + Attention-based BiLSTM multimodal classifier
datasets: Authors’ Multimodal Amharic News Dataset – 23,856 Facebook news stories
sota_baselines: CNN(image)+CNN-BiLSTM(text); CNN(image)+BiLSTM(text); CNN(image)+CNN(text)
summary: The authors first construct a new Amharic text-image fake-news dataset from Facebook. Text is cleaned, normalized, tokenized, and represented using pretrained Amharic FastText embeddings. The strongest textual branch uses an attention-based BiLSTM, while images are resized to 100×100, converted to grayscale, enhanced using CLAHE, denoised with a median filter, and processed using a CNN. The two independently trained modality branches are combined using late fusion with concatenation, followed by dense/classification layers for binary real/fake prediction. Four multimodal configurations are evaluated, with CNN for images + attention-based BiLSTM for text giving the strongest reported result.

title: Interpretable and robust multimodal fake news detection with evidence fusion and reliable reasoning
positive_applications: trustworthy social-media moderation; uncertainty-aware content screening;
ethical_concerns: Multimodal misinformation can influence public opinion, incite violence, undermine democratic institutions, and use misleading images/text combinations to make deceptive claims appear credible
detection_limitations:
Can still produce confidently incorrect predictions for ambiguous/adversarial inputs; cross-modal conflict can increase error/uncertainty; evaluated mainly on text-image data, so audio/video and multilingual generalization remain untested; domain-shift uncertainty calibration and scalability to dynamic social media remain challenges.
 Future work: variable modality dropout, better conflict resolution/evidential fusion, audio/video extension, adversarial robustness, temporal/user context, multilingual/domain adaptation, and more nuanced misinformation classes.
robustness:
1) Dempster–Shafer Theory-based uncertainty-aware gated fusion dynamically resolves conflicts between semantic and pattern evidence rather than treating all features equally.
2) Joint correlation refinement + bidirectional cross-attention explicitly models text-image consistency, while evidential/contrastive losses improve calibration and robustness to ambiguous/OOD inputs.
data_collection:
Fakeddit: Existing public Reddit text-image dataset; >1M original samples, with a curated binary subset of 33,000 used here; no synthetic generator used by authors.
Twitter Fake News / image-verification corpus: existing public social-media text-image dataset with binary real/fake labels; no synthetic generator used by authors.
detection_models: TrustFND
sota_baselines: BERT; Swin-T; EANN; SpotFake+; SAFE; CAFE; MRML; EANBS; CLIP+LoRA
summary: TrustFND extracts two complementary representations from each modality: BERT provides text pattern/context features while CLIP-Text supplies semantic features; Swin-T extracts image pattern/spatial features while CLIP-Image supplies semantic visual features. Within each modality, semantic and pattern information are dynamically combined using a gated fusion mechanism, followed by Dempster–Shafer Theory-based evidence fusion to quantify belief, uncertainty, and feature conflict. The text and image representations are then enhanced using joint correlation refinement and bidirectional multi-head cross-attention, allowing text to attend to images and images to attend to text. The two cross-attended representations are concatenated and classified, while an evidential head estimates prediction uncertainty. Training combines classification, evidential, contrastive, supervised-contrastive, and uncertainty-regularization losses.

title: A rigorous interrogation of multimodal fake news detection paradigms: adversarial robustness and modality dependence
positive_applications: trustworthy social-media/news verification; benchmarking resilience to generative-AI attacks.
ethical_concerns: disinformation that undermines public trust and democratic processes.
detection_limitations:
All evaluated models remain vulnerable to adversarial attacks, particularly LLM-based text attacks; several architectures show strong dependence on the visual modality; D1 contains watermark artifacts that encourage shortcut learning.
Future work: more advanced end-to-end/vision-transformer models, larger LLM attackers such as GPT-4o/Llama-70B, watermark-masked retraining, attacks from native multimodal generative models, adversarial training, and fusion strategies robust to noisy/missing/adversarial modalities.
robustness: This paper does not propose a new robustness module. Its contribution is a systematic robustness framework: 10 image attacks + 7 text attacks, including Llama3/DeepSeek attacks, black-box transfer attacks, modality ablation, Grad-CAM failure analysis, and evaluation across three datasets with different distributions.
data_collection:
D1: Existing benchmark, 4,843 samples (2,613 fake/2,230 true), many fake images contain explicit “FAKE” watermarks.
RECOVERY: Existing dataset, 1,445 samples (310 fake/1,135 true), COVID/recovery-related misinformation. PolitiFact: Authors curated ~3,000 claim-text + associated primary image/meme pairs from PolitiFact fact-check articles; ~35% fake/misleading. No synthetic generator used to create these datasets.
detection_models: LongBERT-VGG; CNN-VGG; LSTM-VGG; BERT-CLIP; ViLBERT
sota_baselines: LongBERT-VGG; CNN-VGG; LSTM-VGG; BERT-CLIP; ViLBERT
summary: The study benchmarks five representative multimodal fake-news detectors: LongBERT-VGG, CNN-VGG, LSTM-VGG, BERT-CLIP, and ViLBERT. The first four use separate text and image encoders followed by attention-based late fusion, while ViLBERT performs deeper text-image interaction through co-attentional Transformer layers. The models are trained separately on D1, RECOVERY, and PolitiFact, then stress-tested using 10 image attacks and 7 text attacks, including Llama 3- and DeepSeek-generated semantic/grammar attacks. The study also performs text-only/image-only modality ablation, black-box transfer attacks, Grad-CAM error analysis, statistical significance testing, and computational-cost analysis to understand robustness and modality dependence.

title: A unified multimodal large model framework for cross-platform fake news spread chain detection
positive_applications: Cross-platform misinformation tracing; chain-level fake-news detection; moderation; forensic analysis; early warning; identification of influential spread nodes and cross-platform links.
ethical_concerns: Cross-platform misinformation can be re-authored, amplified, and redistributed across ecosystems. The paper also warns that detection systems themselves could be misused for censorship or surveillance, so it recommends transparent deployment and human-in-the-loop verification.
detection_limitations:
Relies on observable propagation data, so private messages/deleted or ephemeral content create missing links; sophisticated deepfakes and adversarial perturbations remain difficult; real-time large-scale deployment is computationally demanding.
Future work: add video/audio, temporal dynamics for early warning, federated/privacy-preserving learning, stronger annotated cross-platform benchmarks, and improved robustness to adversarial/deepfake content.
robustness:
1) Platform adapters + cross-modal contrastive alignment reduce platform-specific semantic drift and improve leave-one-platform-out generalization.
 2) Chain-level relation-aware graph reasoning aggregates propagation evidence across posts/platforms, making detection less dependent on any single transformed post.
data_collection:
FakeNewsNet: public PolitiFact/GossipCop news + social context.
Fakeddit: public Reddit text-image posts.

summary: EFCV first extracts image entities using Faster R-CNN and text entities using spaCy, then encodes both global and entity-level information into a common 512-D space using CLIP ViT-B/16. In the consistency view, bidirectional cross-modal attention and a Transformer produce coarse-, fine-, and entity-level representations, which are dynamically fused using a learned gate. In parallel, the visual clue view reweights image/text features using entity importance and processes them through a Transformer to capture scene, object-relation, and visual-style cues.
