title: Emulating Reader Behaviors for Fake News Detection
positive_applications: Social-media fake-news detection; misinformation verification; content credibility assessment; detection of inconsistencies among headline, image, comments, and article body.
ethical_concerns: Rapid misinformation dissemination, misleading users through manipulated or mismatched multimedia content
detection_limitations:
Performance varies substantially across different fake-news categories; designing one detector that performs equally well across all categories remains difficult. Missing components also affect performance—for example, some datasets lack body text or images.
Future work: category-specific fake-news detection and better explanation of why a sample is fake
robustness:
1) Ember models news at the component level rather than only modality level, allowing it to adapt to datasets with different available components.
2) Inter-component co-attention + sequence-based aggregation explicitly learns relationships among every pair of components following reader verification behavior, improving generalization across fake-news categories/domains.
data_collection:
GossipCop: real-world celebrity/gossip fake news from fact-checking sources; no synthetic generator reported.
PolitiFact: real-world political fake news; no synthetic generator reported.
Fakeddit: Reddit-based fake news with Satire; Misleading Content; Manipulated Content = manual photo editing; False Connection = text-image mismatch; Imposter Content = bot-generated content; no specific GAN/LLM generator reported.
detection_models: Ember – Emulating the Behaviors of Readers
datasets: FakeNewsNet: GossipCop, PolitiFact2, PolitiFact7; Fakeddit subsets: Satire, MisCon, ManCon, FalCon, ImpCon, Compre
sota_baselines: HAN; Text_CNN; dEFEND; HMCAN; CAFE; SAFE
summary: Ember models fake-news detection by imitating how readers consume and verify news. It separately encodes four components—headline, image, comments, and body text—using component-specific feature extractors. Text components are represented with GloVe embeddings and recurrent attention networks, while images use ELA + ResNet50 to capture semantic and tampering-related information. Every pair of components is then compared using parallel co-attention, and these pairwise representations are arranged according to the typical reading sequence—headline → image → comments → body—and aggregated using a GRU. The resulting representation is used to classify the news as real or fake.

title: Enhancing large language model for fake news video detection via cross-modal retrieval
positive_applications: misinformation verification,
ethical_concerns: difficult to detect and enabling rapid deceptive information spread
detection_limitations:
Strong dependence on high-quality related news; removing related news reduces accuracy by 5.7 percentage points. LLM hallucinations still occur despite truthfulness constraints. Large models were not fine-tuned on fake-news-video data because of computational limits.
Future work: improve crawling/data sources, use RAG to reduce hallucinations, and fine-tune LLMs on misinformation datasets.
robustness:
1) Information-Bottleneck-based keyframe extraction removes redundant video frames while preserving task-relevant information, reducing video noise.
2) Cross-modal retrieval + three-view LLM prompt reasoning combines related video, related text, and generated contextual knowledge instead of relying only on the target video.
data_collection: FakeSV: existing real-world Chinese short-video dataset from Douyin/Kuaishou, constructed from fact-checking events and containing 1,827 fake + 1,827 real + 1,884 debunking videos. Current authors additionally collected 4,875 related textual news articles using event descriptions to search fact-checking websites and official media; FakeSV debunking videos are used as related video evidence. No synthetic generator was used by these authors
detection_models: FVDLM – Enhanced Method for Fake Video Detection based on Cross-modal Retrieval with Large Models
sota_baselines: Faster R-CNN+Attention; VGGish; Wu et al.; FANVM; SV-FEND; SV-FEND+NEED; Qwen2-VL; LLaVA-OV
summary: FVDLM first retrieves related video and textual news for the target video. It then applies an Information Bottleneck-based keyframe selector, using VGG frame features and BiLSTM temporal modeling, to remove redundant frames. Selected video information is transformed into textual/symbolic knowledge using subtitles/OCR and Qwen2-VL, while Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct generates contextual information such as key-event descriptions, sentiment, stance, and supplementary knowledge. Three prompt branches then judge authenticity using similar real/fake training examples, generated knowledge context, and retrieved related news. Their predictions, confidence levels, and explanations are combined through majority-confidence logic or an additional LLM decision selector to produce the final real/fake label.

title: Entity Graph Alignment and Visual Reasoning for Multimodal Fake News Detection
positive_applications: Multimodal misinformation verification; social-media content authentication;
ethical_concerns: Deceptive multimodal content can exploit image-text combinations to increase credibility, obscure important visual details, mislead users, and threaten reliable information dissemination and societal safety.
detection_limitations: The paper does not provide a dedicated limitations/future-work section. It does identify important remaining challenges in this area: LVLMs can miss subtle visual details and spatial relationships and may hallucinate unseen objects; low-quality/compressed images, hashtags, watermarks, and other social-media noise can disrupt alignment. CMA-VRP is specifically designed to reduce these problems
robustness:
1) Entity-level graph contrastive alignment learns fine-grained text-image relationships and remains effective when entities are missing or ambiguous.
2) Adversarial Cycle-Consistent Invariant Learning maps text and visual representations into a shared modality-invariant space, reducing noise-induced semantic drift and improving robustness to noisy/unaligned data.
data_collection:
Twitter/MediaEval: Real-world text-image misinformation; misleading/mismatched multimedia content; no synthetic GAN/LLM generator reported.
Pheme: Real-world social-media rumor/news verification with text + images; no synthetic generator reported.
Weibo: Real-world Chinese text-image fake news; no synthetic generator reported.
detection_models: CMA-VRP – Cross-Modal Alignment with Visual Reasoning Prompting
sota_baselines: BERT; ResNet34; MVAE; CFFN; Event-Radar; InfoSurgeon; COOLANT; LLaVA; LLaVA + SPT; NLIN
summary: CMA-VRP constructs separate textual and visual entity graphs from each text-image news pair. Textual entities and relations are obtained using dependency parsing and BERT, while visual entities and relationships are extracted using a Mask R-CNN-based scene graph generator, with Rosetta OCR adding text appearing inside images. The framework then uses Mistral-7B and LLaVA-1.6-13B with truth-driven chain-of-thought prompting to produce visual reasoning features describing actions, scenes, entities, and their relevance to the claim. Inter- and intra-graph contrastive learning aligns fine-grained entities across modalities, followed by graph-based cross-modal fusion. Finally, a CycleGAN-style adversarial cycle-consistent alignment learns modality-invariant representations from text and image features, and the combined representation is passed through a fully connected Softmax classifier for real/fake prediction.

title: Event Consistency-aware Robust Fake News Detection
positive_applications: Short-video misinformation detection; content verification on TikTok/Kuaishou-like platforms; detection of edited/re-purposed news videos; identification of manipulated audio narratives; robust video content moderation.
ethical_concerns: Creators can re-edit authentic news, insert unrelated material
detection_limitations: EVDL can fail when an AI-generated fake video is highly semantically aligned with its accompanying text because there are no obvious event-irrelevant segments to remove. The authors explicitly identify AI-generated fake-news detection as an important future direction. Highly similar consecutive video segments can also make relevant/irrelevant segment separation difficult
robustness:
1) EVDL uses text as a factual/event anchor plus LLM-generated contextual descriptors to remove event-irrelevant/noisy video segments.
2) ATCM explicitly calculates text-audio inconsistency and upweights inconsistent audio regions, making subtle tampered audio information more detectable.
data_collection:
FakeSV: Real-world Chinese short-video fake news; 5,538 manually annotated videos covering 738 events; 1,827 fake + 1,827 real + 1,884 debunking videos; no specific synthetic generator reported.
FakeTT: Real-world TikTok short-video fake news collected from events fact-checked by Snopes; 1,172 fake + 819 real; includes video, audio and text; manipulation includes re-edited content/audio tampering, and at least one AI-generated-video case is reported, but exact generator is not specified
detection_models: ECR-FND – Event Consistency-aware Robust Fake News Detection
sota_baselines: TikTec; SV-FEND; NEED; FakingRecipe; HML; OpEvFake; GPT-3.5; Qwen2-VL; LLaVA-OV; GPT-4o-mini; DeepSeek-R1
summary: ECR-FND is a three-modality short-video fake-news detector using text, video, and audio. CLIP extracts textual and video semantic features, XLM-RoBERTa extracts textual sentiment, VGGish extracts audio semantics, and HuBERT extracts audio sentiment. The Event-aware Video Denoising Learning (EVDL) module uses the text as a factual anchor, enriched with DeepSeek-R1-generated contextual descriptors, to compute text-video consistency and remove event-irrelevant video segments. The Audio Tampering-information Capturing Module (ATCM) compares textual and audio semantics, inverts the consistency scores to emphasize inconsistent regions, and amplifies likely audio tampering cues. Predictions from the denoised video/text branch and audio-tampering branch are finally combined using late fusion for real/fake classification.

title: Explainable Cross-Modal Consistency Learning with Social Graph Neural Networks for Multimodal Fake News Detection
positive_applications: Social-media misinformation monitoring; content verification; multimedia forensics; detection of manipulated images; propagation-aware early fake-news detection; explainable decision support.
ethical_concerns: Misinformation, manipulation of public perception, erosion of trust, political/social instability,
detection_limitations:
Current framework is evaluated on text-image-social graph data rather than deepfake video; real-time multilingual deployment is not addressed; model complexity may limit edge/mobile deployment.
Future work: real-time multilingual misinformation detection, deepfake video analysis, reinforcement-learning-based adaptive detection, and lightweight edge architectures.
robustness:
1) Contrastive representation learning + Cross-Modal Consistency Learning explicitly aligns coherent text-image pairs and detects semantic contradictions.
2) Temporal/social graph modeling captures propagation dynamics, supporting cross-dataset and changing-pattern generalization.
data_collection:
ISOT: fake-news dataset; generation/manipulation model not specified in this paper.
WELFAKE: fake-news dataset; no GAN/LLM generator reported.
TRUTHSEEKER: misinformation/social-media dataset; no synthetic generator reported. Image manipulation is analyzed through image-forensic features, but exact source generators are not given.
detection_models: Explainable Cross-Modal Consistency Learning Framework with Temporal Social GNN
sota_baselines: CNN-based model; BERT model; SpotFake; GNN-based model
summary: The proposed framework combines multilingual transformer-based text encoding (BERT/XLM-R) with ViT-based visual representation, followed by contrastive representation learning to align text and image semantics. A Cross-Modal Consistency Learning (CMCL) module uses cross-attention to explicitly detect semantic agreement or contradiction between the two modalities. In parallel, a Temporal/Social Graph Neural Network models reposting, commenting, sharing, and other propagation behavior. The multimodal and graph representations are fused and classified with fully connected layers and Softmax, while SHAP, attention visualization, and graph explanations provide interpretability.

title: FACT-CLIP: Fake News Detection via CLIP-Based Cross-Modal Attention and Transformer Fusion
positive_applications: Social-media fake-news detection; misinformation verification; multimedia content authenticity checking
ethical_concerns: Misinformation can confuse public opinion, cause financial loss, social disruption,
detection_limitations:
Computationally expensive because of large transformer/CLIP architecture; high GPU and memory requirements; evaluated on only one dataset; CLIP may assign high similarity to contextually related but still fake images, limiting deeper semantic reasoning.
Future work: larger datasets, more explainability, and fine-tuning CLIP for more efficient fake-news detection.
robustness:
1) Combines global image features, entity-level visual features, and CLIP cross-modal embeddings instead of relying on a single visual representation.
2) Attention-weighted transformer fusion captures deeper text-image semantic interactions and reduces noisy/redundant multimodal features.
data_collection:
Twitter/MediaEval “Verifying Multimedia Use”: real-world text-image misinformation; no GAN/LLM/deepfake generator reported.
Manipulation includes text-image mismatch, misleading text with real images, unrelated images with real text, and cases where both text and image are fake.
detection_models: FACT-CLIP
feature_extraction:
Text: multilingual-BERT + CLIP Text Encoder;
Image: ResNet-152 + Faster R-CNN + CLIP ViT-B/32; Fusion: Attention + Transformer Encoder;
sota_baselines: EANN; SpotFake; BDANN; FNR
summary: FACT-CLIP processes the textual modality using multilingual-BERT and the CLIP text encoder, while the image modality is represented using ResNet-152 for global visual features, Faster R-CNN for entity-level features, and CLIP ViT-B/32 for aligned image embeddings. CLIP cosine similarity is used to quantify text-image correspondence. The textual, visual, and CLIP-derived features are passed through separate projection heads, dynamically weighted by an attention mechanism, and then fused using a custom Transformer encoder to model deeper multimodal semantic interactions. A linear classifier finally predicts real or fake news.

title: Fake News Detection Based on Cross-Modal Ambiguity Computation and Multi-Scale Feature Fusion
positive_applications: misinformation filtering
ethical_concerns: mislead the public, create economic losses and social unrest
detection_limitations:
The semantic-consistency module uses cosine similarity between BERT embeddings, but BERT’s anisotropic embedding space reduces similarity accuracy.
Future work: improve semantic-consistency measurement and extend the multi-scale/cross-modal method to additional modalities such as audio and video.
robustness:
1) Spatial + frequency-domain image modeling captures both semantic content and physical tampering/compression traces.
 2) Cross-modal semantic-consistency measurement plus Co-Attention helps detect cases where text and image appear individually plausible but contradict each other.
data_collection:
Weibo: Existing Chinese text-image dataset; 7,850 samples (4,211 positive, 3,639 negative); true news verified by Xinhua, fake news from Weibo and the national rumor-refuting platform; no synthetic generator used by authors.
English/Twitter news: Existing text-image dataset; 5,669 samples (2,825 positive, 2,844 negative); fake news from Kaggle/BS Detector covering 244 fake-news websites, authentic news from reputable outlets such as The New York Times. Authors filtered samples to retain items containing both text and image.
detection_models: MFFFND-Co – Multimodal Feature Fusion Fake News Detection with Co-Attention Block
datasets: Weibo; English News / Twitter image-verification dataset
sota_baselines: Bi-LSTM; BERT; VGG19; att-RNN; MVAE; MKEMN; CAFE; MCAN; MFFFND
summary: MFFFND-Co extracts textual semantics using BERT, image spatial information using VGG19, and image frequency-domain tampering/compression traces using DCT-CNNs. A first Co-Attention block combines image spatial and frequency representations. The resulting visual representation is then fused with text through another Co-Attention block to form the text-image joint representation. Separately, an image-captioning API converts the image into text, which is encoded with BERT and compared with the original news-text embedding using cosine similarity to obtain a semantic-consistency score. The consistency score is concatenated with the fused text-image representation and passed to a fully connected Softmax classifier for real/fake prediction.

title: Fake News Detection Based on Cross-Semantic Multimodal Data Fusion
positive_applications: Social-media fake-news detection; multimodal content verification; media credibility improvement; information-integrity protection.
ethical_concerns: damage trust in media, threaten personal and societal security
detection_limitations: The paper mainly evaluates one dataset, so broader cross-dataset/domain generalization is not demonstrated. The method also depends on K-Means cluster quality and manually selected cluster count, and uses relatively heavy BERT/VGG-19 feature extraction. Explicit future-work discussion is limited in the paper.
robustness:
1) Local + global semantic feature modeling captures both overall news semantics and cluster-specific local patterns
. 2) Co-Attention explicitly learns bidirectional text-image interactions instead of simple concatenation, improving multimodal consistency modeling
data_collection: Biendata fake-news dataset: real-world text-image news collected up to 2019 and expanded through web crawling; no specific GAN/LLM/deepfake generation model reported
detection_models: CSMDF – Cross-Semantic Multimodal Data Fusion model
sota_baselines: EANN; MVAE; SAFE; MCAN; FSRU
summary: CSMDF first extracts global semantic features from text using BERT and from images using VGG-19. It then uses K-Means clustering and center-loss-based optimization to obtain local semantic features for each modality. Global and local features are combined through BiGRU to form cross-semantic text and visual representations. A Co-Attention module then models bidirectional interactions between the two modalities, and the fused representation is passed to cluster-specific MLP binary classifiers for final real/fake prediction.

title: Fake News Detection Using Speech-to-Text and Chinese BERT

summary: MFMDF performs binary few-shot misinformation detection using paired textual and visual content. summary: The NTSG framework takes paired news body text and images as input and models both internal narrative coherence and cross-modal consistency. RoBERTa-base encodes the text, which is divided chronologically into head, body, and tail segments; mean-pooled segment representations are used to calculate semantic offset vectors that capture narrative transitions and logical breaks. ResNeSt-50 extracts visual feature maps, while a narrative probe constructed from the textual semantic offsets and global representation guides cross-modal saliency alignment to emphasize image regions relevant to the evolving narrative. Enhanced textual and visual representations are projected into a shared 768-dimensional space and dynamically combined through a multimodal gated fusion layer. The fused representation is classified as real or fake using an MLP with ReLU, Dropout, and Softmax. Experiments are conducted on the PolitiFact and GossipCop subsets of FakeNewsNet.

summary: SepVAMark embeds separable audio–visual watermarks using UNet-like encoders and MLP-based feature fusion. A robust bimodal decoder traces sources, while modality-specific semi-robust decoders reveal tampering through watermark errors. FakeAVCeleb experiments evaluate media quality and resilience to benign and deepfake attacks.

title: SparseMoE-MFN: A Sparse Attention and Mixture-of-Experts Framework for Multimodal Fake News Detection on Social Media
positive_applications: Social-media misinformation/rumor detection; multilingual content moderation;
ethical_concerns: mislead users, affect public discourse, health, and safety
detection_limitations: Potential bias inherited from pretrained models; fixed Top-K expert selection may limit adaptability; cross-lingual transfer needs deeper study; deployment on resource-constrained devices remains challenging; adversarial robustness and OCR-noise robustness are not fully addressed; distinguishing semantically close classes such as rumor vs. unverified still needs improvement. Future work includes dynamic Top-K routing, stronger cross-lingual transfer, adversarial/OCR robustness, and better fine-grained semantic reasoning
robustness:
1) Top-k sparse bidirectional cross-modal attention suppresses irrelevant text/image regions and reduces noisy cross-modal links.
2) Sparse MoE routing dynamically sends representations to visual, language, or cross-modal alignment experts, improving adaptation to heterogeneous and ambiguous inputs; load-balancing and expert dropout further reduce over-reliance on one expert.

MR2-E from Twitter (English) = 6,976 posts; total 14,700 image-text posts. Labels: 3,172 rumor, 4,927 non-rumor, 6,601 unverified. Dataset also provides comments, user profiles, timestamps and social context, but current SparseMoE-MFN primarily uses image-text pairs. No synthetic generator used by the authors.
detection_models: SparseMoE-MFN
sota_baselines: EANN; HFM; MVAE; LLaVA-v1.6; Qwen2-7B; MiniGPT-4; UniVL

summary: SPGR suppresses irrelevant multimodal noise with learned semantic masks and measures joint text–video–audio conflict through Gramian volume. Geometry and purified semantics guide a two-stage mixture of experts before classification. FakeSV and FakeTT experiments include component, routing, and loss ablations.

title: Toward Explainable Multimodal Fake News Detection: A Fusion of Prompt Learning and Automated Machine Learning
positive_applications: Early-stage fake-news identification; transparent explanations supporting trustworthy decisions.
ethical_concerns: Deliberately misleading readers; societal harm from misinformation.
detection_limitations: Sparse/low-quality text and fixed fusion weights can reduce performance; future open-source LLaMA 3 and instance/dataset-adaptive fusion.
robustness: ChatGPT-4.0 Domain/Few-shot Prompts + XGBoost Guidance + 16 Hand-crafted Image Features + Fuzzy C-Means + AutoGluon Weighted Ensemble + Cosine-basis Functional Network + SHAP/LIME
data_collection: Public Twitter, PolitiFact, Buzzfeed, FNID text; CASIA V2, CoMoFoD, FID, FIDAC image-forgery data. Multimodal evaluation uses Twitter/PolitiFact/Buzzfeed; no new fake-content collection/generation.
metrics: Accuracy; Precision; Recall; F1; training/inference time; explanation Identity, Separability, Stability; Morris sensitivity indices.
detection_models: Unnamed explainable AutoML–LLM framework — hybrid ML/DL pipelines with backend Functional Network decision fusion.
datasets: Twitter; PolitiFact; Buzzfeed; FNID; CASIA V2; CoMoFoD; FID; FIDAC.
feature_extraction: Text: prompted ChatGPT with metadata, few-shot examples, keywords, general knowledge, XGBoost predictions. Image: intensity (gray level/skewness/uniformity), texture (statistics/GLCM/LBP), shape (area/perimeter/ratios/roughness) → FCM + AutoGluon. Fusion: output scores → additive cosine-basis FN.
sota_baselines: ETMA; DSF-MHSA; MFIR; MRAN; CAFE; MCNN; SpotFake; LSTM-ATT; SAMPLE; QMFND; ITS; MDF-FND; C3N; EANN; AMFB; MVAE; AutoKeras; TPOT; k-means; hierarchical clustering; GMM.
summary: The framework combines prompted ChatGPT text classification with an image pipeline using hand-crafted features, fuzzy clustering, and AutoGluon. An interpretable Functional Network fuses modality outputs, while SHAP/LIME and textual justifications explain decisions. Experiments cover text, image-forgery, and multimodal news datasets.

title: Toward Generalizable Deepfake Detection via Forgery-Aware Audio–Visual Adaptation: A Variational Bayesian Approach
modalities_raw: Audio, Video; text manipulation in evaluated IDForge data.
positive_applications: Deepfake forensics for live streaming and social-media sharing.
ethical_concerns: Harmful misinformation; reputational damage; cheating in cyberspace.
detection_limitations: Compression damages temporal clues; failures with multiple/stationary speakers, occluded lips, extreme poses; lacks temporal localization and explicit text modeling.
robustness: Frozen ViT Backbones + Global-Local Forgery-aware Difference Convolutions/FFT High-pass Filters + Gaussian Variational Bayesian Estimation + Modality/Correlation Variable Factorization + Orthogonality Constraint + Adapter Addition + Classification Heads
data_collection: Existing FakeAVCeleb, KoDF, DeAVMiT (from VidTIMIT), DFDC, LAV-DF, IDForge videos. Frames at 5 fps/MTCNN; audio at 16 kHz. LAV-DF forged segments extracted; problematic IDForge faces excluded.
detection_models: FoVB — parameter-efficient audio–visual DL detector with frozen backbones and learned adapters.
datasets: FakeAVCeleb; KoDF; DeAVMiT; DFDC; LAV-DF; IDForge.
feature_extraction: Video: MTCNN facial crops → ViT patches. Audio: STFT/log-Mel spectrogram → ViT patches. GLFA: ADC/CDC/RDC/SOC + FFT high-pass features; VBFE: Gaussian shared/specific codes → projection/addition to Transformer features.
sota_baselines: LipForensics; FTCN; RealForensics; MDS; AV-DFD; AVoiD-DF; MCL; PVASS-MDD; AVFF; FRADE; PIA; Xception; AVAD (LRS2/LRS3); ICSAV.
summary: FoVB adapts frozen audio–visual Transformers with local difference convolutions and global high-frequency filters. Variational Bayes estimates disentangled modality-specific and correlation-specific Gaussian variables, which are added back into the backbone. Evaluation examines dataset/manipulation transfer, perturbation robustness, and adapter ablations.

title: Towards Tamper-Resistant Digital Media: An AI and Blockchain Approach for Deepfake Detection
positive_applications: Journalism authenticity; forensic investigation; social-media verification; law enforcement; digital-rights management.
ethical_concerns: Misinformation; impersonation; identity theft; privacy/security threats.

detection_models: Unnamed AI–Blockchain multimodal framework — DL detection frontend and blockchain verification backend.

SHA-256 fingerprints and Ethereum smart contracts preserve detection records for later verification. Experiments use visual and audio deepfake benchmarks, although architecture descriptions vary between sections.

title: Transformer-Based Natural Language Processing for Fake News Detection in Social Media Platforms
positive_applications: Real-time social-media monitoring/moderation; supporting moderators with interpretable outputs; detecting misleading memes/marketing.
ethical_concerns: Misleading users and affecting social, political, and economic conditions.
detection_limitations: Annotated-data dependence; computational demands at scale; evolving misinformation. Future semi/self-supervised learning, lightweight/distilled edge models and continual learning.
robustness: BERT/RoBERTa + Hierarchical Text Aggregation + OCR + ViT + Parameter-efficient Adapters + Bidirectional Cross-modal Attention + Contrastive InfoNCE/ITM/MLM + Classification Head + Saliency
data_collection: Public fake-news/meme datasets plus API streams/ethical scraping; MinHash/LSH deduplication; crowd labeling followed by expert adjudication; time/source splits. Evaluation names Weibo, Twitter, Bahasa-Indonesia.
metrics: Accuracy; Precision; Recall; F1; AUC (evaluation protocol); Cohen’s kappa (annotation agreement).
detection_models: CrossAlign — multimodal Transformer DL framework with adapter tuning.
datasets: Weibo; Twitter; Bahasa-Indonesia dataset; additional collected corpora unnamed.
feature_extraction: Text: BERT/RoBERTa subword embeddings + chunk attention pooling; embedded image text: OCR. Images: ViT/CLIP visual backbone (ResNet/Faster R-CNN alternative). Fusion: asymmetric bidirectional cross-attention + contrastive alignment → dense Softmax/sigmoid head.
sota_baselines: P. Yang et al. multimodal Transformer; S. F. N. Azizah et al. BERT/ALBERT/RoBERTa study.
summary: CrossAlign combines contextual text, image patches, and OCR cues with cross-modal attention and contrastive alignment. Hierarchical aggregation handles long text, while adapters reduce tuning cost and saliency supports moderation. Results compare methods on Weibo, Twitter, and a Bahasa-Indonesia text-only benchmark.

title: TrueLens Video Fake News Detection with Dual Level Evidence Gathering and Consolidation
positive_applications: Reliable evidence and guidance for human verification in high-stakes scenarios.
ethical_concerns: Emotionally persuasive, rapidly spreading video misinformation.
detection_limitations: Future: integrate MLLMs throughout evidence gathering/consolidation for fine-grained reasoning and reliable human-readable rationales.

data_collection: FakeSV: Douyin/Kuaishou; FakeTT: TikTok, Snopes verification; FVC: YouTube/Facebook/Twitter. Sixteen keyframes with aligned audio, titles, keywords and ASR; temporally separated events. Reference memory contains training samples only; retrieves real/fake evidence.
metrics: Accuracy; Macro-F1; Macro-Precision; Macro-Recall; NLL/calibration; Hit@1; informativeness, contextualization and evidence-specificity scores; training time; GPU memory; significance p-values.

sota_baselines: BERT; ViT; Wav2Vec; TikTec; FANVM; CAFE; SV-FEND; FakingRec/FakingRecipe; REAL; ExMRD.
summary: TrueLens enriches short videos with MLLM-derived themes/storylines and retrieves real/fake reference evidence using entropy-guided uncertainty. Dual attention heads contrast supporting and contradicting evidence, and Dirichlet outputs are combined using Dempster–Shafer fusion. Evaluation covers three video-news datasets, retrieval quality and calibration.

title: Two-Stage Knowledge Distillation Network With Multi-Teacher Self-Training for Semi-Supervised Multi-Modal Fake News Detection
positive_applications: Social-media credibility verification with reduced annotation requirements.
ethical_concerns: Erroneous judgments; mental/financial losses; social panic and disorder.
detection_limitations: Focuses on missing labels; future cross-domain evaluation and a domain-robust module. Difficult pseudo-labels have higher error rates.
robustness: BERT + CLIP + Information-bottleneck Distillation Encoder + Attention-weighted Fusion + Two Self-training Teachers/Adaptive Confidence + Gaussian Consistency + Semantic/Structural Distillation + True/Pseudo-label Joint Supervision + Student MLP
data_collection: Weibo: real Xinhua news and official debunked posts (May 2012–January 2016). Fakeddit: Reddit subset (30k train/10k test). Pheme: Twitter text/image pairs re-collected from linked images. FakeSV: Douyin/Kuaishou video-news; varied labeled-data ratios simulate label scarcity.
metrics: Accuracy; Precision; Recall; Macro-F1; pseudo-label accuracy; McNemar-test p-values; training time; FLOPs; parameter count.
detection_models: TKDN — semi-supervised multimodal DL teacher–student knowledge-distillation framework.

sota_baselines: HMCAN; CAFE; MRML; ALGM; QMFND; SV-FEND (additional video experiment).
summary: TKDN trains two teachers through adaptive-confidence self-training and noise-based consistency. Semantic and structural distillation transfer their multimodal representations to a student, followed by joint supervision from factual and consensus pseudo-labels. Experiments vary annotation ratios across three text–image datasets and additionally test FakeSV videos.

title: Unified semantic-aware reasoning for fake news video detection
positive_applications: Fake-news video verification
ethical_concerns: spread realistic misinformation, damage public trust, and affect public safety.

Future work: optimize encoder architectures, develop more efficient video-context modeling, and improve adaptability to emerging manipulation techniques.
robustness:
1) CACR performs bottom-up object→frame→segment reasoning to capture fine-grained manipulation clues rather than relying on global video features.
2) VSCT uses adaptive gating to dynamically weight static visual and dynamic audio-text features according to semantic relevance, improving adaptability across different manipulation patterns
data_collection:
FakeTT: Public TikTok fake-news video dataset covering 91 events; 1,991 videos total = 819 real / 1,172 fake.
FMNV: Public Twitter + YouTube fake-news video dataset; 2,393 videos total = 893 real / 1,500 fake. Authors did not create either dataset and do not report generating fake samples themselves.
detection_models: USAR – Unified Semantic-Aware Reasoning
sota_baselines: Qwen2-VL, GPT-4o , SV-FEND, FakingRec, FMNVD, USAR

title: Unifying Vision and Language for Robust Fake News Detection Using Novel Deep Samples

data_collection: Fakeddit Reddit headlines paired with images; missing/duplicate/misaligned samples removed. Balanced 50,000-sample subset split 40,000/5,000/5,000 for train/validation/test; text normalized/tokenized and images resized.

BERT/MobileNetV2, CLIP and DistilBERT/EfficientNet-B0 produce modality embeddings that are concatenated and classified by MLPs. Classification metrics, confusion matrices and learning curves evaluate performance; reported accuracies are inconsistent across sections.

title: Unleashing the Potential of Consistency Learning for Detecting and Grounding Multi-Modal Media Manipulation
positive_applications: Protecting information security and user privacy; detecting and locating manipulated news content.
ethical_concerns: Fake media threatens information security and user privacy.
detection_limitations: Depends on distinguishable genuine/forged features; too few selected patches/tokens under-model cues, while too many introduce irrelevant content. No explicit future work.
robustness: ViT-B/16 + RoBERTa (METER initialization) + Six-layer Co-attention + Contextual Consistency Decoder + Semantic Consistency Decoder + Forgery-aware Reasoning/Aggregation + MLP Classification/Bounding-box Heads + Text Threshold Filter
data_collection: Existing DGM4 news pairs from The Guardian, BBC, USA TODAY and The Washington Post: 77,426 genuine and 152,574 manipulated. Manipulations: face swap, face attributes, text swap and text attributes; image/text/both forged with region/token annotations.

datasets: DGM4 (including image-only and text-only manipulation subsets).
feature_extraction: Image: ViT patches; Text: RoBERTa tokens; co-attention aligns modalities. Three self-attention layers and pairwise cosine consistency model local context; cross-modal semantic consistency guides reliable/suspicious attention aggregation. Concatenated CLS features classify; local features ground forgery.
sota_baselines: TS; MAT; BERT (table typo: BETR); LUKE; CLIP; ViLT; HAMMER; HAMMER++; ViKI; UFAFormer; Wang et al. (ICASSP 2024 modality-specific framework).

Supervised consistency matrices guide reasoning over reliable/suspicious content. Separate heads classify authenticity/manipulation types and ground forged faces, while a semantic threshold identifies edited words on DGM4.

title: Vision-Audio based Deepfake Detection according to Multi-modal Learning
positive_applications: Generation: training-data augmentation, language translation, metaverse creation. Multimodal detection: biometrics, user identification and multimedia analysis.

data_collection: FakeAVCeleb real/fake videos with real-real, real-fake, fake-real and fake-fake modality pairs. 810/90/90 train/validation/test samples; celebrities do not overlap across splits; 10-fold validation tests unseen identities.

title: XFake: Leveraging Cross Lingual Vision Multi-Encoder Representations for Accurate Fake News Detection in Multilingual Social Media

English Fakeddit and Chinese WeiboNet pairs undergo augmentation and a combined train/validation/test split.
